title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 17
paragraphs: Beginning with the trading station of the Borysthenites—for of all the places along the sea this is the central point of Scythia—beginning here, the first regions are occupied by the Callipidai, who are Hellenic Scythians; and above these is another people called the Alazonians. These last, and the Callipidai, in all other respects have the same customs as the Scythians, but they sow corn and use it for food, as well as onions, leeks, lentils, and millet. Above the Alazonians dwell Scythians who till the ground, and these sow their corn not for food but to sell.

Beyond them dwell the Neuroi; and beyond the Neuroi, towards the north wind, is a region without inhabitants so far as we know. These peoples are along the river Hypanis, to the west of the Borysthenes. After crossing the Borysthenes, the first region from the sea-coast is Hylaia, and beyond this, as one goes up the river, dwell agricultural Scythians, whom the Hellenes who live on the river Hypanis call Borysthenites (though they call themselves citizens of Olbia). These agricultural Scythians occupy the region extending eastwards for a three days' journey, reaching as far as a river called the Panticapes, and northwards for eleven days' sail up the Borysthenes. Immediately beyond these the desert begins and extends a great distance; and on the other side of the desert dwell the Androphagoi, a people apart, having no connection with the Scythians. Beyond them begins a region that is truly desert and has no race of men in it, so far as we know.
